blockers.title: A device that never opened on both courses keeps the course given up: refused changes with names in uploadRefusals, its rows in free pages, and its students on screen until reopened
blockers.evidence: src/persistence/migrations.ts:144-153 sets the mark only when an open finds n > 1, and settleSeveralCourses returns when it is unset. courseLeftThisDevice (:113-125) is false because the kept course is present. src/App.tsx:958-962 reloads only on courseLeftWithBackup or secondCourseArrived, and both are false after a swap from one course to another. A phone or PC closed during the two-course window holds only course Y. The server now holds only X, so its first checkpoint removes Y and adds X together and n never reaches 2. Its unsent Y changes are refused while Y is still here, so src/persistence/uploadRefusals.ts courseStillHere keeps them. Output of the swap case: 'SWAP courses: 1'; 'SWAP uploadRefusals: 1 with the name: true'; 'SWAP marks: []'; 'SWAP raw storage, the given-up student: true'; 'SWAP raw storage, the refused student: true'. Control, a device that opened on both: 'CONTROL uploadRefusals: 0', and both raw storage checks false. 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md (B7 paragraph) says 'the next open clears their refused changes and free pages'; on this device it does not. Riprova cannot clear them either (uploadRefusals.ts:238-242, parentsPresent); only 'Togli dall'elenco' removes the refusal, and nothing removes the free pages.
blockers.reproduction: My scratchpad's r1/garante.spec.ts, test 'swap: a device that never held both'. Fake backend, synthetic students. The student upload is answered 42501, as the access rules answer a child of an erased course. The checkpoint is simulated by one write transaction on ps_data__synced_* that removes Y and adds X, the same technique as downloadRemoves in tests/e2e/b7-two-courses.spec.ts. That a real checkpoint applies removal and arrival together is reasoned from PowerSync's behaviour, not run live. Suggested direction: decide on what is gone, not on whether n > 1 was seen. For example record the bound course id, and on any open where it has left, drop refusals of absent courses and compact; also reload when the bound course has left.
blockers.specRef: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md B6 success predicate (nothing of the removed course remains readable on the device); B7 success predicate (every device opens on that one course); 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md B7 paragraph; precedent SP-B6-1, SP-UG3-1

blockers.title: A compaction cut short after the choice is never finished: the mark is deleted before the VACUUM and no pending record is written
blockers.evidence: src/persistence/migrations.ts:154-160 deletes local:several-courses in a committed transaction, then runs compactCourseDatabase(...).catch(() => {}). It never writes COMPACTION_PENDING_ID, which the import writes in its transaction (src/persistence/courseArchive.ts:162-165) so that the next open finishes (migrations.ts:270-271, the fix for review DI-UG3-1). Closing the app, or a VACUUM failure, in that window leaves the given-up course in free pages for good. Output: 'CUT marks after the cut: []'; 'CUT after two more opens, raw storage, the given-up student: true'.
blockers.reproduction: My scratchpad's r1/garante.spec.ts, test 'cut: the compaction does not end after the mark is deleted'. For one open the route serves src/persistence/writeGuard.ts with the VACUUM call replaced by a rejection, which leaves the same state as an app closed before the VACUUM commits. The route is then removed and the app reopened twice. Fix: write COMPACTION_PENDING_ID in the transaction that deletes the mark.
blockers.specRef: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md B6 success predicate; 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md B7 paragraph; precedent DI-UG3-1

blockers.title: keep_course erases every other course of the owner, including courses the device never showed and the owner never named
blockers.evidence: supabase/migrations/20261104000000_keep_course.sql:25-30 collects all the owner's courses and :38-39 deletes every one except keep_id, with no active filter and no list of what the owner saw. src/backup/session.ts:623-625 sends only keep_id. src/features/courseChoice/CourseChoiceScreen.tsx:203-221 names only the courses on this device. A course Z uploaded by a third device, or by a device that erased Y offline and made a new course, is erased irreversibly if the choosing device's download has not delivered it. That window is real: PowerSync applies no checkpoint while this device's queue is not empty (the wait at session.ts:618-622 lasts up to 30 s), and the owner's phone has shown a stalled download with working uploads (session.ts:329-335). The owner's confirmation and tick name only Y. Second defect in the same function: under READ COMMITTED the DELETE at :38 takes a new snapshot, so a course committed after the SELECT at :25 is deleted without an erased_courses row (:35-37 uses the older array) and can be uploaded back. Inactive rows go the same way, unseen; I found no live path that creates one (src/persistence/courses.ts:53 runs only from the no-course screen). The fake backend repeats the same rule (tests/e2e/b7-two-courses.spec.ts:75-80), so the suite cannot catch this.
blockers.reproduction: Reasoned from the SQL as the brief allows; no Postgres is available and I did not execute it. Steps on a development backend with synthetic accounts: (1) the account holds X and Y and device A shows both; (2) with A's download held, insert course Z with a student through a second session; (3) call keep_course(X) from A; (4) expected: Z stays or the choice is refused because the set changed; from the SQL, Z and its student are gone. Fix: pass the ids given up, for example keep_course(keep_id, give_up text[]). Refuse with a distinct code if the owner's set differs from keep_id plus give_up, and delete with c.id = any(given-up ids) so the record and the delete cover the same rows.
blockers.specRef: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md B7: 'The app shows both courses and the owner chooses which to keep; it never erases one by itself'

importantFindings.title: Signed in or offline, the choice screen offers no Esci and no reset
importantFindings.evidence: src/features/courseChoice/CourseChoiceScreen.tsx:457 and :512 render OnlineBackup only when signed out or on another account. A read-only device has no buttons at all (:175). The B7 section of 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md names 'Impostazioni, Esci, export and reset are out of reach' as the defect. On a shared or handed-over phone the session keeps syncing two courses of minors, and offline nothing can remove them. Not a blocker: the success predicate and the approved mock do not ask for Esci.

importantFindings.title: After the server answers, the course given up stays readable and exportable on the choosing device until a download arrives, and the screen says nothing was erased
importantFindings.evidence: src/backup/session.ts:599-606 erases nothing locally and no local record of the choice exists. Close the app after 'Scelta salvata' and reopen offline: readCourseChoices shows both courses again with Salva file, under 'Non è stato cancellato nulla' (CourseChoiceScreen.tsx:470-472). The confirmation said 'sarà eliminato da questo telefono'. If the session is lost before the download, it never leaves. Tapping the course given up returns CVGON, so no harm to the server. tests/e2e/b7-two-courses.spec.ts:270 pins the two courses before the download; the later reopen is read from code, not run.
importantFindings.reproduction: Keep a course with the backend answering, set the browser offline before any download, reload, and read the screen.

importantFindings.evidence: src/features/settings/CourseFiles.tsx:311-313 says 'Il file contiene i dati personali degli allievi... solo con persone autorizzate'. src/features/courseChoice/CourseChoiceScreen.tsx:79-118 and :232-244 download immediately with no such text, including for the 'Salva prima' copy of a course about to be erased. The file name itself is clean: code, week, year and the first 8 characters of a random id (:62-65).

importantFindings.title: The live test 'no account may call it' cannot detect a missing revoke
importantFindings.evidence: tests/e2e/b7-two-courses-live.spec.ts:349-361 accepts any 4xx. If anon held EXECUTE, auth.uid() would be null, owned empty, and the function would answer CVGON with 400, so the test would pass. src/persistence/backendSchema.test.ts checks only the text of the revoke. Assert the refused-by-privilege answer instead (code 42501, status 401 from PostgREST), not merely a 4xx.
importantFindings.reproduction: Read the assertion against the SQL at supabase/migrations/20261104000000_keep_course.sql:31-34.

importantFindings.title: Unsent changes of the course given up go to the server first, while the owner is told they will be lost
importantFindings.evidence: src/backup/session.ts:618-622 waits for the whole queue. CourseChoiceScreen.tsx:227-229 says 'andrà persa'. tests/e2e/b7-two-courses.spec.ts:425 records queuedRows: 3 reaching the server before the erase. Names never online then reach Supabase and the replication stream only to be erased, and stay in the provider's copies for up to 7 days. The general provider sentence (:232-234) does not tell the owner this applies to them.
importantFindings.reproduction: tests/e2e/b7-two-courses.spec.ts 'unsent changes are shown on their course and go up before the choice'.
